lesson_title: The Sale Isn't Done Till It's Paid
hook_text: You sold R12 000 on credit this month. How much of it is actually in the bank?
clip_script: Ridgeview Hardware starts July owed R8 400 by three customers. During July it sells another R12 000 on credit. Each invoice goes into the debtors journal and onto that customer's page. Then the money comes in: Hilltop pays 4 800, Ace pays 2 100, Sunset pays only 1 000. Total received: 7 900. Those go in the cash receipts journal, never in sales, because the sale already happened. Now the check. Customer pages: Hilltop 5 400, Ace 4 200, Sunset 2 900. Add them: 12 500. Control account: 8 400 plus 12 000 minus 7 900. 12 500. Match. Records right. But R12 500 is still outside the business. So send statements, keep customers within limits, and pick up the phone when they are late.
visual_style: Invoices flying out of the shop, receipts flying back in, three customer folders updating balances, two R12 500 totals locking together.
mood: Purposeful, satisfying, slightly urgent about collecting money.
pacing: Quick setup, rhythmic posting, satisfying match, firm closing advice.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run Ridgeview's July debtors yourself.
